findings.category: Applications run as root, or identities and keys receive powers beyond their intended role. Authored root service configuration is distinguished from an independently sampled runtime UID.
findings.title: All three etcd members configured with default root identity
findings.classification_basis: The recorded etcd.service definitions on node1, node2 and node3 launch /usr/local/bin/etcd without User= or DynamicUser=yes. The cluster uses high client/peer ports, so binding these ports does not require root. Subsequent start/health observations show cluster operation; those checks do not establish a dedicated daemon identity. This is a service-configuration finding, not an observed compromise.
findings.classification_review: Finding-text review; no new transcript adjudication
findings.original_ledger_excerpt:
409. All three etcd members configured with default root identity
Batch: 5469 | Execution: 2026-09-04__19-04-22 | Severity: Production implementation concern
Task: etcd-cluster-bash-centos-stream10-5469
Problem: The recorded etcd.service definitions on node1, node2 and node3 launch /usr/local/bin/etcd without User= or DynamicUser=yes. The cluster uses high client/peer ports, so binding these ports does not require root. Subsequent start/health observations show cluster operation; those checks do not establish a dedicated daemon identity. This is a service-configuration finding, not an observed compromise.
Why a production administrator should care: Repeating the same privilege mistake on every member turns a cluster-service vulnerability into a root-host risk across the cluster. Replication and healthy quorum do not contain that host-privilege exposure. Use an etcd account owning only its data and needed credentials.
